title: Scalar extension commutes with inverse image on independently sized sites
statement: Let $C$ and $D$ be sites essentially small in a module universe $u$, with independent object and morphism universes. Let $F:\operatorname{Sh}(C,\mathrm{Set}_u)\to\operatorname{Sh}(D,\mathrm{Set}_u)$ have right adjoint $V$ and preserve finite limits. Let $a_Y:A_Y\to B_Y$ and $a_X:A_X\to B_X$ be maps of sheaves of commutative rings. Specify algebraic inverse images $I_A,I_B$ for $F$ with coefficient pairs $(A_Y,A_X),(B_Y,B_X)$ [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image], and assume their underlying ring isomorphisms make the coefficient square commute. For module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], let $T_Y$ and $T_X$ be any left adjoints of restriction of scalars along $a_Y$ and $a_X$, with units $\eta_Y$ and $\eta_X$. There is a natural isomorphism $e:I_B\circ T_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}T_X\circ I_A$. Writing $\iota_I:F(|M|)\xrightarrow{\sim}|I(M)|$ for the inverse of the specified underlying-module comparison, it obeys $F(|\eta_{Y,M}|);\iota_{I_B,T_Y(M)};|e_M|=\iota_{I_A,M};|\eta_{X,I_A(M)}|$. No exactness or coefficient-flatness hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback: adjunction proof of the inverse-image/scalar-extension comparison, with the operation transport of Tags 03D2 and 03D7

proof.text: Transport direct-image additive groups and module actions through the right adjoint V, using finite-product comparison isomorphisms. The adjunct of the ring inverse-image isomorphism is a ring homomorphism by naturality of the adjunction and the ring-operation graph equations. Restriction along this adjunct gives a functor P on BX-modules and its underlying set-sheaf comparison.

Transpose maps from IA(M) to a restricted BX-module through F left adjoint to V. The binary-operation mate equations show that additivity and scalar linearity on the two sides are equivalent; the coefficient square supplies the scalar-action mate equation. Faithfulness of the forgetful functors restricts the set-sheaf equivalence to module hom sets, naturally in both variables. Applying this also to IB and the identity coefficient maps gives the second Hom equivalence.

Compose these Hom equivalences with the adjunctions for TY and TX. The two composite functors are left adjoints to the same right adjoint. The unique adjunction comparison is therefore a natural isomorphism. Its equation under the Hom equivalence, together with the underlying transpose equation, is precisely the stated unit normalization.

Mathlib module-sheaf pullback and localization APIs do not identify the specified arbitrary algebraic inverse images with their continuous-site specializations. The existing scalar-inverse-image tower theorem has same-universe sites.

theorem exists_scalarInverseImageIndependent
{SY : Type uC} {SX : Type uD} [Category.{vC} SY] [Category.{vD} SX]
  [EssentiallySmall.{u} SY] [EssentiallySmall.{u} SX]
  {JY : GrothendieckTopology SY} {JX : GrothendieckTopology SX}
  {AY BY : Sheaf JY CommRingCat.{u}} {AX BX : Sheaf JX CommRingCat.{u}}
  (F : Sheaf JY (Type u) ⥤ Sheaf JX (Type u))
  (V : Sheaf JX (Type u) ⥤ Sheaf JY (Type u))
  (adj : F ⊣ V) [PreservesFiniteLimits F]
  (IA : AlgebraicInverseImage F AY AX) (IB : AlgebraicInverseImage F BY BX)
  (aY : AY ⟶ BY) (aX : AX ⟶ BX)
  (ha : F.map ((sheafCompose JY (CategoryTheory.forget CommRingCat.{u})).map aY) ≫
    IB.ringUnderlying.hom = IA.ringUnderlying.hom ≫
      (sheafCompose JX (CategoryTheory.forget CommRingCat.{u})).map aX)
    (TY : SheafOfModules.{u}
        ((sheafCompose JY (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj AY) ⥤
      SheafOfModules.{u}
        ((sheafCompose JY (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj BY))
    (TX : SheafOfModules.{u}
        ((sheafCompose JX (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj AX) ⥤
      SheafOfModules.{u}
        ((sheafCompose JX (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj BX))
    (adjY : TY ⊣ restrictScalars.{u}
      ((sheafCompose JY (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).map aY))
    (adjX : TX ⊣ restrictScalars.{u}
      ((sheafCompose JX (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).map aX)) :
    ∃ e : TY ⋙ IB.modules ≅ IA.modules ⋙ TX,
      ∀ M : SheafOfModules.{u}
          ((sheafCompose JY (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj AY),
        F.map ((toSheaf
          ((sheafCompose JY (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj AY) ⋙
            sheafCompose JY (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u})).map
              (adjY.unit.app M)) ≫
          IB.moduleUnderlying.inv.app (TY.obj M) ≫
            (toSheaf ((sheafCompose JX (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj BX) ⋙
              sheafCompose JX (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u})).map (e.hom.app M) =
          IA.moduleUnderlying.inv.app M ≫
            (toSheaf ((sheafCompose JX (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj AX) ⋙
              sheafCompose JX (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u})).map
                (adjX.unit.app (IA.modules.obj M))
